listing.name: Performance Improvements Using OpenJ9 JRE
listing.summary: I have been experimenting with using different JREs to run StarSector, and OpenJ9 seems to improve fps and RAM usage.
listing.aiSummary: Improves game performance by replacing the default Java runtime with OpenJ9.

description:
Summary
I have been experimenting with using different JREs to run StarSector, and OpenJ9 seems to improve fps and RAM usage. For those who don't know what a JRE is, they are responsible for running Java programs (ie StarSector), many organizations have their own version of them, and they affect performance. Running the Graphics Lib benchmark, OpenJ9 achieved an average of 42.5 fps, while OpenJDK (the one that comes with the game) achieved 32.5. On a memory benchmark, OpenJ9 used an average of 1205 MB of RAM, while OpenJDK used 1313 MB. I have also tried Hotspot and GraalVM, but the results weren't promising. I might make a better installation guide in the future. If anyone manages to install and run the game with OpenJ9 successfully, sharing information on bugs and performance would be appreciated.

OpenJ9 Installation

Download install scripts from https://github.com/itBeABruhmoment/starsector-openj9/releases/download/v0.2.0/starsector-openj9.zip
Download OpenJ9 from https://developer.ibm.com/languages/java/semeru-runtimes/downloads/. Version 23.0.2.0 was used for this guide but other versions likely work
Find the path to your Starsector installation location. The default is "C:\Program Files (x86)\Fractal Softworks\Starsector"
Copy the path to the OpenJ9 zip you downloaded
In an admin prompt, run .\windows_openj9_install.bat "C:\Path\To\Starsector" "C:\Path\To\some-prefix-openj9-some-version.zip"
Run the game with "Starsector\starsector-core\j9_starsector.bat"

OpenJ9 Uninstallation

Download install scripts from https://github.com/itBeABruhmoment/starsector-openj9/releases/download/v0.2.0/starsector-openj9.zip
Find the path to your Starsector installation location. The default is "C:\Program Files (x86)\Fractal Softworks\Starsector"
In an admin prompt, run .\windows_openj9_uninstall.bat "C:\Path\To\Starsector"

FPS Experiment

Spoiler
Set Up:
OpenJDK (default) vs OpenJ9. OpenJ9 ran with default garbage collector and -Xaggressive
Windows 11 system, 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1235U, x86-64 core, integrated graphics
4096 megabytes of RAM, 1280x800 resolution
Game set to "real time" priority in the task manager
Console Commands and Graphics Lib mods enabled, Graphics Lib shaders disabled

Experiment:
Start the game
Run the Graphics Lib benchmark mission for 2 minutes to warm up the JVM
Run the Graphics Lib benchmark mission for 2 minutes three times and collect the result of each run

Results:

OpenJ9:
Average FPS: 42.1, 42.7, 42.6
Minimum FPS: 18.8, 20.2, 21.1
Frame Variance (ms): 3.51, 2.57, 3.53
Average Frame Variance (ms): 4.78, 4.97, 4.66
Average Memory Used (GB): 0.64, 0.64, 0.69

OpenJDK:
Average FPS: 32.2, 31.8, 33.3
Minimum FPS: 19.8, 17.4, 20.8
Frame Variance (ms): 4.51, 7.54, 1.56
Average Frame Variance (ms): 5.69, 6.87, 6.06
Average Memory Used (GB): 1.80, 1.75, 1.67

*The RAM figures here likely don't have any relation to actual memory efficiency. The game's heap gets a fixed amount of space and unused memory is wasted memory. In actuality, a 300 MB heap can run the benchmark.

RAM Experiment

Spoiler
Basic Rationale:
There are components of the JVM beyond the heap that take up a significant amount of memory. This test aims to check OpenJ9 has more memory efficient implementations of these components. As a result, each JVM was limited to 300 MB of heap space, which is about the minimum amount needed to run the benchmark.

Set Up:
OpenJDK (default) vs OpenJ9. OpenJ9 ran with default garbage collector and -Xaggressive
Windows 11 system, 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1235U, x86-64 core, integrated graphics
300 megabytes of RAM, 1280x800 resolution
Console Commands and Graphics Lib mods enabled, Graphics Lib shaders disabled

Experiment:
Start the game
Load a campaign save (pre-made, new game) and run the game for 4 minutes
Run the Graphics Lib benchmark mission for 2 minutes
Record memory usage according to the task manager
Repeat three times

Results (MB):

OpenJ9:
1215, 1212, 1188

OpenJDK:
1316, 1311, 1313
